children: Shares of Factorial Energy climbed after the company said it would partner with Mitsui Kinzoku to scale its all-solid-stade battery manufacturing capabilities.
The stock rose 12%, to $5.58, on Thursday. Shares debuted on the Nasdaq Stock Market in June, following the completion of Factorial's business combination with Cartesian Growth Corporation III.

"It's driven by the entire supply chain and, increasingly, by an entire industry coalition," Chief Executive Siyu Huang said, adding that Factorial partnered with Mitsui because battery innovation can't be done by a single company:

Mitsui produces sulfide-based solid electrolytes for all-solid-state batteries, and it is one of only a few companies worldwide with foundational technology in the space, according to Factorial. The company also produces ultra-thin copper foil, with an estimated 90% share of the semiconductor market for the material.

The combination of Mitsui's expertise in materials and manufacturing technologies and Factorial's advanced technological capabilities will help to accelerate the realization of next-generation batteries, the companies said.
